# Event-level splicing with rMATS-turbo {#sec-rmats}

@sec-cryptic worked with junctions one at a time. Event-level tools take
the next step: they group junctions and exons into **splicing events** and
test whether the proportion of transcripts that include an exon changes
between conditions. rMATS [@shen2014] is one of the most widely used; its
current implementation, rMATS-turbo, is described in detail by
@wang2024. This chapter explains what rMATS computes, shows the exact
command we ran on the demo data from @sec-strand, and spends most of its
time on **reading the output correctly**, which is where most mistakes
happen.

```{r}
#| label: setup
source("R/helpers.R")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)
})
```

## What rMATS models

rMATS knows five event types. Each event has an *inclusion* form and a
*skipping* form:

| Event | Inclusion form | Skipping form |
|---|---|---|
| SE, skipped (cassette) exon | upstream - **exon** - downstream | upstream - downstream |
| A5SS, alternative 5' splice site | longer exon (downstream donor) | shorter exon |
| A3SS, alternative 3' splice site | longer exon (upstream acceptor) | shorter exon |
| MXE, mutually exclusive exons | contains the first exon | contains the second exon |
| RI, retained intron | intron kept | intron spliced out |

For every event and sample, rMATS counts reads that support each form:

- **IJC** (inclusion junction count) and **SJC** (skipping junction count).
- In the **JC** output only reads that span a splice junction are counted.
  In the **JCEC** output, reads that fall entirely inside the alternative
  exon body are added to the inclusion count. JCEC has more reads, but exon
  body reads are also affected by things other than splicing (coverage
  bias, overlapping features), so the two are reported **separately** and
  should be kept separate.

Because the inclusion form usually has more possible read positions than the
skipping form, rMATS normalises by the "effective lengths" `IncFormLen` and
`SkipFormLen`:

$$
\hat{\psi} = \frac{\text{IJC}/\text{IncFormLen}}{\text{IJC}/\text{IncFormLen} + \text{SJC}/\text{SkipFormLen}}
$$

$\hat\psi$ (percent spliced in, PSI) is reported per sample as `IncLevel1`
and `IncLevel2`. The test asks whether the mean PSI differs between the two
groups by more than a small cut-off, using a hierarchical model that
accounts for both read sampling and variation between replicates, and the
p-values are converted to FDR with the Benjamini-Hochberg method.

::: {.callout-important}
## Which group is which
`IncLevelDifference = mean(IncLevel1) - mean(IncLevel2)`, where 1 is the
`--b1` group and 2 the `--b2` group. We used **b1 = TDP-43 knockdown** and
**b2 = scramble**, so a **positive ΔPSI means more inclusion in the
knockdown**. Always write this down; with the groups swapped, every sign in
the table flips.
:::

## The command

The inputs are two text files that list the BAM files of each group
(comma-separated), and a GTF. Every option reflects something we measured
or decided earlier:

```bash
# b1.txt: knockdown BAMs, b2.txt: scramble BAMs (comma-separated, one line)
rmats.py \
  --b1 b1.txt --b2 b2.txt \
  --gtf work/demo/ref/panel.gtf \   # GENCODE v26, the same annotation as everywhere else
  -t paired \                       # paired-end library (chapter 2)
  --readLength 76 \                 # real read length (chapter 2)
  --libType fr-unstranded \         # measured, not assumed (chapter 4)
  --novelSS \                       # we are looking for unannotated (cryptic) splice sites
  --nthread 4 --od work/demo/rmats --tmp work/demo/rmats_tmp
```

Why these options matter:

- **`--readLength`** must be the real read length. rMATS uses it to compute
  effective lengths, and by default it ignores reads of a different length.
  If your reads were trimmed to different lengths, add
  `--variable-read-length`; if the aligner soft-clips reads, add
  `--allow-clipping` (we avoided both by aligning with `--no-softclip`).
- **`-t paired`** or **`-t single`** must match the library.
- **`--libType`** comes from @sec-strand.
- **`--novelSS`** lets rMATS build events from splice sites that are not in
  the GTF. Without it, an exon defined by two novel splice sites, which is
  exactly what a cryptic exon is, cannot be found. Use it when you are
  looking for novel or cryptic events; for a standard analysis of annotated
  events, leave it off, since it adds many low-confidence events and makes
  the multiple-testing correction harsher.

The group files used for the demo:

```{r}
#| label: groups
cat("b1 (TDP-43 KD):", gsub(",", "\n   ", readLines("data/demo/rmats/b1.txt")), "\n")
cat("b2 (scramble): ", gsub(",", "\n   ", readLines("data/demo/rmats/b2.txt")), "\n")
```

## The output files

```{r}
#| label: files
list.files("data/demo/rmats", pattern = "MATS")
```

There is one file per event type, in two versions (JC and JCEC). rMATS also
writes intermediate files (`fromGTF.*`, `JC.raw.input.*` and others) that we
do not need here.

```{r}
#| label: summary-file
read.delim("data/demo/rmats/summary.txt") |>
  knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE)
```

## Reading the tables: by column name, never by position

The five event types do not have the same columns. SE, A5SS, A3SS and RI
describe one alternative region, but MXE describes **two** alternative exons
and therefore has two more coordinate columns:

```{r}
#| label: columns
se  <- read.delim("data/demo/rmats/SE.MATS.JC.txt")
mxe <- read.delim("data/demo/rmats/MXE.MATS.JC.txt")
names(se)
names(mxe)
c(FDR_column_in_SE = which(names(se) == "FDR"), FDR_column_in_MXE = which(names(mxe) == "FDR"))
```

A filter written as `awk '$20 < 0.05'` therefore filters FDR in the SE file
but a completely different column in the MXE file, and nothing warns you.
Filter by **column name**, in R or pandas, and the same code works for every
event type.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Coordinates in rMATS output are 0-based
`exonStart_0base` is 0-based, as the name says, while `exonEnd` is the
1-based end. The exon in normal 1-based coordinates is
`exonStart_0base + 1` to `exonEnd`. Forgetting this puts every exon one base
off when you compare with GTF or recount3 coordinates.
:::

A reader that works for every event type:

```{r}
#| label: reader
read_rmats <- function(event, count_type, dir = "data/demo/rmats") {
  f <- file.path(dir, sprintf("%s.MATS.%s.txt", event, count_type))
  x <- read.delim(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if (nrow(x) == 0) return(NULL)
  # IJC_SAMPLE_1, SJC_SAMPLE_1, ... hold comma-separated per-replicate values
  split_sum <- function(a, b) {
    mapply(function(i, s) as.numeric(strsplit(i, ",")[[1]]) + as.numeric(strsplit(s, ",")[[1]]),
           a, b, SIMPLIFY = FALSE)
  }
  reads_g1 <- split_sum(x$IJC_SAMPLE_1, x$SJC_SAMPLE_1)
  reads_g2 <- split_sum(x$IJC_SAMPLE_2, x$SJC_SAMPLE_2)
  x$mean_reads_per_sample <- mapply(function(a, b) mean(c(a, b)), reads_g1, reads_g2)
  x$event_type <- event
  x$count_type <- count_type
  x
}
```

## Filtering

Our predefined filter, applied to the JC and JCEC results separately:

- **FDR < 0.05**,
- **|ΔPSI| > 0.1** (`abs(IncLevelDifference) > 0.1`),
- **at least 10 informative reads per sample on average**: the mean over all
  samples of IJC + SJC must be at least 10. Events with very few reads can
  produce extreme PSI values from a handful of reads.

```{r}
#| label: filter
events <- c("SE", "A5SS", "A3SS", "MXE", "RI")
all_events <- lapply(c("JC", "JCEC"), function(ct)
  bind_rows(lapply(events, read_rmats, count_type = ct)))
names(all_events) <- c("JC", "JCEC")

apply_filter <- function(x) {
  x |>
    mutate(pass_fdr = FDR < SPLICE_FDR,
           pass_dpsi = abs(IncLevelDifference) > SPLICE_DPSI,
           pass_reads = mean_reads_per_sample >= 10,
           significant = pass_fdr & pass_dpsi & pass_reads)
}
filtered <- lapply(all_events, apply_filter)

bind_rows(filtered) |>
  group_by(count_type, event_type) |>
  summarise(tested = n(),
            FDR_only = sum(pass_fdr),
            FDR_and_dPSI = sum(pass_fdr & pass_dpsi),
            all_filters = sum(significant), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE)
```

The read filter matters: some events reach a low FDR with very few reads.
Note that the multiple-testing family here is **the events in our 17-gene
panel**, not the genome. An FDR from a targeted panel is not comparable with
an FDR from a genome-wide run; say which one you report.

## The significant events

```{r}
#| label: sig-events
sig_jc <- filtered$JC |>
  filter(significant) |>
  mutate(exon = case_when(
    event_type == "SE" ~ paste0(chr, ":", exonStart_0base + 1, "-", exonEnd),
    event_type == "MXE" ~ paste0(chr, ":", X1stExonStart_0base + 1, "-", X1stExonEnd,
                                 " or ", X2ndExonStart_0base + 1, "-", X2ndExonEnd))) |>
  arrange(FDR)
sig_jc |>
  transmute(event_type, gene = geneSymbol, strand, exon,
            `PSI KD (per sample)` = IncLevel1, `PSI scramble (per sample)` = IncLevel2,
            dPSI = IncLevelDifference, FDR = formatC(FDR, format = "e", digits = 1),
            mean_reads = round(mean_reads_per_sample)) |>
  knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(sig_jc, "results/rmats_demo_significant_JC.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

rMATS writes an FDR of exactly 0 when the value is below its numerical
precision; read it as "very small", not as certainty. How to read the table:

- The same exon can appear in several rows (here *MADD*), once for each
  combination of flanking exons that rMATS found. When you count results,
  count **exons**, not rows.
- Two of the strongest events are **annotated** exons that are skipped more
  often in the knockdown (negative ΔPSI). One is in *POLDIP3*, a gene whose
  splicing is known to change when TDP-43 is lost [@shiga2012]; the other is
  in *KCNQ2*, and it is the same event that appeared in @sec-cryptic as a
  "known sites, new pair" junction: the skipping junction joins two
  annotated splice sites that GENCODE v26 never pairs.
- The others are **cryptic** exons with positive ΔPSI (*KALRN*, *GRAMD1A*,
  *EPB41L4A*, *MADD*): almost never included in scramble, included in a
  fraction of transcripts in the knockdown. These are the exons that needed
  `--novelSS`.

## Do rMATS and the junction analysis agree?

@sec-cryptic paired novel junctions into candidate cassette exons. If rMATS
works as intended, the cryptic exons in our panel genes should appear as
significant SE events with a positive ΔPSI (more inclusion in the
knockdown). We match them by their 1-based coordinates.

```{r}
#| label: compare
ce <- read.csv("results/cryptic_exons_paired.csv")
# rMATS can report the same exon several times, once for each pair of
# flanking exons. Keep the best-supported event (smallest FDR) per exon.
se_jc <- filtered$JC |> filter(event_type == "SE") |>
  mutate(exon_start = exonStart_0base + 1, exon_end = exonEnd) |>
  group_by(chr, exon_start, exon_end) |>
  slice_min(FDR, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()
panel <- readLines("scripts/demo_genes.txt") |> grep(pattern = "^#", invert = TRUE, value = TRUE)
ce |>
  filter(gene %in% panel) |>
  left_join(se_jc |> select(chr, exon_start, exon_end, IncLevelDifference, FDR,
                            mean_reads_per_sample, significant),
            by = c("chrom" = "chr", "exon_start", "exon_end")) |>
  transmute(gene, exon = paste0(chrom, ":", exon_start, "-", exon_end), exon_length,
            found_by_rMATS = !is.na(FDR), dPSI = round(IncLevelDifference, 3),
            FDR = ifelse(is.na(FDR), NA, formatC(FDR, format = "e", digits = 1)),
            mean_reads = round(mean_reads_per_sample),
            significant) |>
  knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE)
```

Most cryptic exons from @sec-cryptic are found by rMATS as SE events, all
with a positive ΔPSI, but only one passes every filter in this small demo.
The reasons are instructive:

- **ΔPSI too small.** The *AGRN* cryptic exon has a tiny FDR and plenty of
  reads, but it is included in only a few percent of transcripts, so ΔPSI
  stays below 0.1. This is the same pattern that made definition B miss it
  in @sec-cryptic: a rare event in a highly expressed gene.
- **FDR too high.** Some exons (for example in *PFKP* and *SLC24A3*) have a
  ΔPSI just above 0.1 but do not reach FDR < 0.05 with three samples per
  group.

Two broader lessons:

1. **Event models only find what they model.** The main *STMN2* event
   (exon 1 to the cryptic exon 2a, where transcripts end) is not a cassette
   exon, an alternative splice site or a retained intron, so rMATS has no
   event type for it. The junction analysis in @sec-cryptic finds it
   easily.
2. **Depth limits what can be called.** The demo uses 3 samples per group
   from the shallower batch. A cryptic exon that is clear when junction
   reads are summed over 12 samples can miss the read filter or the FDR
   threshold here. That is a statement about power, not evidence that the
   exon is absent.

## Look at the reads

The demo folder contains small BAM slices of the *STMN2* locus for one
knockdown and one scramble sample (`data/demo/igv/`). To look at them:

1. Open IGV [@robinson2011] and select the genome **hg38**.
2. *File > Load from File*, and choose both `.bam` files (the `.bai` index
   files must be in the same folder).
3. Go to `chr8:79,610,500-79,638,500`.
4. Right-click a track and choose **Sashimi Plot** to see junction arcs with
   read counts.

The knockdown track shows reads piling up just downstream of exon 1, inside
intron 1, and split reads joining exon 1 to that region. This is the visual
confirmation that goes together with the junction counts.

## Gene level versus transcript level: DRIMSeq and stageR

rMATS answers questions about **events**. A related question is whether the
relative abundance of a gene's **transcripts** changes (differential
transcript usage). DRIMSeq [@nowicka2016] tests this with a
Dirichlet-multinomial model on transcript-level counts (for example from
Salmon), and stageR [@vandenberge2017] controls the error rate in two
stages: first screen genes, then confirm individual transcripts only within
the genes that passed.

The rule we follow:

> If a gene is significant at the gene level, look for transcript-level
> confirmation with stageR. If no transcript is confirmed, **say so**: the
> gene shows evidence of changed transcript usage, but we cannot say which
> transcript changes.

We did not run DRIMSeq in this book. recount3 does not provide
transcript-level counts, and quantifying transcripts would require the full
reads of every sample. The code below shows the structure of the analysis
for when you have Salmon output; it is not executed.

```{r}
#| label: drimseq-template
#| eval: false
library(DRIMSeq)
library(stageR)

# counts: data.frame with gene_id, feature_id (transcript) and one column per sample
# samples: data.frame with sample_id and condition (scramble as reference level)
d <- dmDSdata(counts = counts, samples = samples)
d <- dmFilter(d, min_samps_gene_expr = 6, min_gene_expr = 10,
              min_samps_feature_expr = 3, min_feature_expr = 10)
design <- model.matrix(~ condition, data = DRIMSeq::samples(d))
d <- dmPrecision(d, design = design)
d <- dmFit(d, design = design)
d <- dmTest(d, coef = "conditionTDP43")

gene_p <- setNames(DRIMSeq::results(d)$pvalue, DRIMSeq::results(d)$gene_id)
tx_res <- DRIMSeq::results(d, level = "feature")
tx_p <- matrix(tx_res$pvalue, dimnames = list(tx_res$feature_id, "transcript"))
stage <- stageRTx(pScreen = gene_p, pConfirmation = tx_p, pScreenAdjusted = FALSE,
                  tx2gene = tx_res[, c("feature_id", "gene_id")])
stage <- stageWiseAdjustment(stage, method = "dtu", alpha = 0.05)
getAdjustedPValues(stage, order = TRUE, onlySignificantGenes = TRUE)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Check your understanding
1. rMATS reports `IncLevelDifference = 0.25` for an exon. In our setup, in
   which group is the exon included more often?
2. Why should JC and JCEC results not be merged into one table?
3. A script filters rMATS output with `awk -F'\t' '$20 < 0.05'` for all five
   event types. What goes wrong?
4. Why can rMATS not detect the main *STMN2* cryptic exon event, even with
   `--novelSS`?
5. An event has FDR = 0.001 and ΔPSI = 0.6 but 4 reads per sample on
   average. How do you report it?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answers
1. In the knockdown: b1 = TDP-43 knockdown and the difference is b1 minus
   b2.
2. They count different things (junction reads only versus junction plus
   exon body reads), so their PSI values and p-values are not
   interchangeable. Report one as the primary analysis and say which.
3. Column 20 is FDR in the SE, A5SS, A3SS and RI files, but not in the MXE
   file, which has two extra coordinate columns. Filter by column name.
4. The cryptic exon 2a ends transcripts at a cryptic polyadenylation site. It
   is an alternative last exon, which is not one of the five rMATS event
   types.
5. It fails the predefined read filter, so it is not reported as
   significant. You may mention it as an exploratory signal that needs more
   depth or targeted validation (for example RT-PCR).
:::
:::
